title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Coverage
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare. They say your coverage will be canceled unless you give them personal information or pay a fee. They may sound very official and urgent.
example_message: "This is Medicare. Your coverage will be canceled unless you confirm your Social Security number and bank account right now."
red_flags: Caller asks for your Social Security or bank information
Threatens to cancel your Medicare coverage
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Tech Support Pop-Ups Lock Your Computer
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer saying you have a virus. It tells you to call a number for help. The person on the phone tries to get remote access to your computer and asks for money.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft Support now at 1-888-XXX-XXXX."
red_flags: Pop-up demands you call a phone number
Claims to be from Microsoft or Apple
Asks for remote access or payment
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number; restart your computer if needed.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: Someone calls pretending to be your grandchild or a police officer. They say your grandchild is in trouble and needs money for bail or an emergency. They ask you to send money right away.
example_message: "Grandma, I’m in jail and need $2,000 for bail. Please don’t tell Mom and Dad!"
red_flags: Caller claims to be a relative in trouble
Wants money sent by wire transfer or gift cards
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member directly to check.

title: Social Security Text Message Scam
how_it_works: You get a text saying there is a problem with your Social Security benefits. The message tells you to click a link or call a number. The scammer tries to steal your personal information.
example_message: "Your Social Security account is locked. Click here to unlock it: [fake link]"
red_flags: Link to click or number to call
what_to_do: Delete the text and do not click any links or call the number.

title: Romance Scams on Social Media
how_it_works: A scammer pretends to be interested in a romantic relationship online. After gaining your trust, they ask for money for an emergency or travel. They often claim to be working overseas.
example_message: "I love you and want to visit, but I need money for a plane ticket. Can you help me?"
red_flags: Asks for money for emergencies or travel
Claims to be overseas and unable to meet in person
what_to_do: Never send money to someone you haven’t met in person.
